questions.question: Which of the following articles of the Indian Constitution is related to the writ of the High Courts?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**226**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• Under Article 226, a writ petition can be filed in a High court for issuing one of the five writs as per the case. 
 
• A High Court is empowered to issue directions, orders, or writs for the enforcement of a Fundamental Right and for any other purpose those include:
 
 
• Habeas corpus
 
• Mandamus
 
• Prohibition
 
• Quo warranto
 
• Certiorari.
 
 
 
• The Supreme Court is considered the protector and guarantor of fundamental rights(Article 32). 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Article 32 of the Indian Constitution has been described as the ‘heart and soul’ of the Indian Constitution by Dr B. R. Ambedkar.

 
 
• It gives a citizen the right to approach the Supreme Court to get resorted to any of the fundamental rights in case of their violation.
 
• It is also known as the Right to Constitutional Remedies.

questions.question: During the reign of which of the following Mauryan kings, the Kalinga War was fought?
questions.solution:

Ashoka

__
 
• Ashoka also is known as "Devanampiya".
 
• Piyadasi was the son of Mauryan Emperor Bindusara and was born in 304 BC.
 
 
• His reign lasted from 268 BC to 232 BC.
 
• Once he became King, he started expanding his empires by conquest, in the ninth year of his reign he waged a war with Kalinga (present-day Odisha).
 
 
 
• Ashoka's 13th Rock edicts describe the Kalinga war.
 
• Source of Information about Ashoka:
 
 
• There are two main sources - 
 
 
• Buddhist sources
 
• Ashoka's edicts
 
 
 
 
 
• Ashoka's inscription can be classified into three - 
 
 
• Pillar edicts
 
• Major rock edicts
 
• Minor rock edicts
 
 
 
• Ashoka uses his name only in four of these places namely 
 
 
• Maski
 
• Brahma Giri (Karnataka)
 
• Gujjara (MP)
 
• Nettur (AP)

• Bindusara was the son of Chandragupta Maurya and father of the King Ashok.
 
• He ascended the throne in 298 BC after his father. 
 
• He had so many names mentioned in the various text.
 
 
 
• Brihadratha
 
 
• The last king of the Maurya dynasty was Brihadratha.
 
• The last Mauryan ruler, Brihadratha, was assassinated in 185 BC by his commander-in-chief, Pushyamitra Sunga.
 
• Sunga Dynasty was established by Pushyamitra Sunga.
 
• Pushyamitra was succeeded by his son Agnimitra, the hero of Kalidasa’s drama Malavikagnimitra.
 
 

 
• Chandragupta Maurya

 
 
• Chandragupta Maurya ascended the throne at the age of 25.
 
• Chandragupta Maurya established the Mauryan Empire by defeating the Nandas.
 
• He defeated the last Nanda ruler Dhanananda and occupied Pataliputra in 322 BC.
 
• Chandragupta Maurya was supported by a wise man named Chanakya/Kautilya.
 
• In 305 BC, Chandragupta Maurya defeated Seleucus Nikator.

questions.question: Who among the following devised a policy that came to be known as the Doctrine of Lapse?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Dalhousie**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__ 

__
 
• The doctrine of Lapse:

 
 
• Lord Dalhousie introduced the Doctrine of Lapse for annexing the dependent states whose ruler died without a natural heir to succeed him.
 
• One kingdom after another was annexed simply by applying this doctrine:** Satara (1848), Sambalpur (1850), Udaipur (1852), Nagpur (1853) and Jhansi (1854).**
 
 
 
• Lord Dalhousie:
 
 
• In 1848, Lord Dalhousie arrived in India as the Governor-General and was determined to extend British rule over India.
 
• Dalhousie occupied the Punjab and Sindh through war and brought several subordinate states directly under the Company’s rule by annexing them on the basis of the Doctrine of Lapse. 
 
• Lord Dalhousie also introduced the Doctrine of Good of Governed under which Awadh (1856) and Punjab (1849) were annexed.
 
• Dalhousie established Public Works Department, the objective behind the formation of this department was the construction and maintenance of canals, roads, bridges, etc.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Lord Canning:

 
 
• Lord Canning served as Governor-General of India from 1856 to 1862.
 
• During his tenure, the Government of India Act, 1858 was passed which created the office of Viceroy to be held by the same person who was Governor-General of India.
 
• Thus, Lord Canning also served as the first Viceroy of India.
 
• The Mutiny of 1857, which he was able to suppress successfully,
 
• The Passing of the Indian Councils Act, 1861 which introduced a portfolio system in India,
 
• Bengal Rent Act (1859).
 
 

 
• Lord William Bentinck (1828-1835):

 
 
• Abolition of sati and other cruel rites (1829).
 
• Suppression of thugi (1830).
 
• Charter Act of 1833.
 
• Resolution of 1835, and educational reforms and introduction of English as the official language.
 
• Annexation of Mysore (1831), Coorg (1834) and Central Cachar (1834).
 
• Treaty of 'perpetual friendship with Ranjeet Singh.
 
• Abolished the provincial court of appeal and circuit.

questions.question: Which of the following Ashokan rock edicts declares prohibition of animal sacrifice?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Major Rock Edict - I**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Major Rock Edict - I** of Emperor Ashoka declares the prohibition of animal sacrifice.
 
• Ashoka, the Mauryan emperor, embraced Buddhism after the Kalinga War and promoted non-violence and compassion towards all living beings.
 
• His edicts were inscribed on rocks and pillars throughout his empire to communicate his policies and ethical guidelines.
 
• These edicts reflect Ashoka's dedication to dharma (moral law) and his efforts to create a just and humane society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ashoka** was one of India's greatest emperors, who ruled almost the entire Indian subcontinent from c. 268 to 232 BCE.
 
• His reign is marked by the spread of Buddhism and the establishment of many stupas and viharas (Buddhist monasteries).
 
• The **Major Rock Edicts** are a series of 14 edicts that provide insights into Ashoka's governance, his dedication to Buddhism, and his efforts to promote moral and ethical living.
 
• These edicts are written in various languages including Prakrit, Greek, and Aramaic, reflecting the diverse linguistic landscape of Ashoka's empire.
 
• Ashoka's legacy continues to be celebrated in modern India, where his symbol, the Lion Capital of Ashoka, is used as the national emblem.

questions.question: What helps making the acidic food alkaline that is coming from the stomach?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bile juice.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Bile juice is secreted by the liver and stored in the gallbladder. It is released into the small intestine when food enters.
 
• Bile neutralizes the acid in chyme, raising its pH and making the intestinal environment more alkaline.
 
• This is a critical step, as the enzymes in the small intestine that further digest food work optimally in an alkaline condition.
 
• Along with neutralizing the acid, bile aids in the emulsification of dietary fat, which helps in its digestion.
 
• It's important to note that excessive bile or reflux of bile into the stomach can cause discomfort and affect the digestive process.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Pepsin:
 
 
• Pepsin is an enzyme that is released in the stomach to break down proteins into smaller peptides during digestion.
 
• It is produced by the chief cells in the stomach lining and is activated by the acidic environment of the stomach.
 
• Pepsin is not involved in making food alkaline, instead, it assists in further breaking down food particles.
 
• Faulty regulation or overproduction of pepsin can lead to peptic ulcers or other gastric disorders.
 
 
 
• Gastric Juice:
 
 
• Gastric juice, a combination of pepsin, hydrochloric acid, and other enzymes, is secreted into the stomach to aid in the digestion of food.
 
• It is acidic in nature, with a pH ranging from 1.5 to 3.5, which is essential for pepsin's protein digestion process.
 
• The acidity of gastric juice also kills many bacteria that enter the stomach, providing a protective function against infection.
 
• Gastric juice is not responsible for making food alkaline, but rather for launching the initial stages of digestion in a highly acidic environment.
 
 
 
• Hydrochloric Acid:
 
 
• Hydrochloric acid (HCl) is one of the main components of gastric juice.
 
• It creates the acidic environment in the stomach needed to activate pepsin and other enzymes.
 
• HCl helps to break down food and kill ingested pathogens.
 
• Like pepsin and gastric juice, hydrochloric acid participates in digestion within the stomach, but it does not play a part in making the chyme alkaline.

questions.question: The Dravidian style of temple architecture can be largely seen from which part of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Southern India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Dravidian style of temple architecture** is predominantly found in the southern states of India, including Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Kerala.
 
• Prominent examples of Dravidian architecture include **Brihadeeswarar Temple** in Thanjavur, **Meenakshi Temple** in Madurai, and **Ranganathaswamy Temple** in Srirangam.
 
• This style is characterized by **pyramidal towers (Gopurams)**, intricate carvings, and elaborate designs on temple walls and pillars.
 
• The architecture flourished under powerful South Indian dynasties like the **Pallavas, Cholas, Pandyas, and Vijayanagara** rulers.
 
• Key features include **large courtyards, mandapas (pillared halls)**, and water tanks within the temple complex.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dravidian Architecture Features:**

 
 
• Gopurams: Monumental entrance towers that dominate the temple's skyline.
 
• Vimana: The sanctum tower built directly above the sanctum sanctorum.
 
• Carvings: Depictions of deities, mythological stories, and intricate designs.
 
• Use of Granite: Most temples were constructed using durable granite stones.
 
 
 
• **Important Dynasties:**
 
 
• **Pallavas:** Early examples like Kailasanathar Temple in Kanchipuram.
 
• **Cholas:** Known for massive temples like Brihadeeswarar Temple.
 
• **Pandyas:** Contributed to the expansion of temple complexes.
 
• **Vijayanagara Empire:** Famous for temples in Hampi.
 
 
 
• **Significance:**
 
 
• Temples served as cultural and religious centers in South India.
 
• They were integral to social life, facilitating festivals, education, and governance.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Sites:**
 
 
• The Great Living Chola Temples (e.g., Brihadeeswarar Temple) are recognized as UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

questions.question: The cells having well - organized nucleus with a nuclear membrane are designated as _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**eukaryotic cells.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Eukaryotic cells are characterized by a well-organized nucleus enclosed by a nuclear membrane.
 
• This is where the cell's DNA is stored.
 
• These cells are generally larger and more complex than prokaryotic cells.
 
• Eukaryotic cells have various types of organelles, including mitochondria, endoplasmic reticulum, and Golgi apparatus, which are enclosed by membranes and have specific functions.
 
• Eukaryotic cells can be found in a wide variety of organisms, including plants, animals, and fungi.
 
• The complex structure of eukaryotic cells allows for compartmentalization and specialization of functions, which enables these cells to perform more complex tasks than prokaryotic cells.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Characteristics
 Eukaryotic Cells
 Prokaryotic Cells
 
 
 
 

 Size
 Generally larger (10-100 μm)
 Generally smaller (1-5 μm)
 
 

 Nucleus
 Present (enclosed by a nuclear membrane)
 Absent (nucleoid area)
 
 

 DNA
 Linear
 Circular
 
 

 Organelles
 Membrane-bound organelles are present
 No membrane-bound organelles
 
 

 Cell division
 Mitosis and meiosis
 Binary fission
 
 

 Organisms
 Plants, animals, fungi, and protists
 Bacteria and Archaea

questions.question: Which Part of the Constitution of India contains within it the powers and functions of the Union Public Service Commission?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Part XIV__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) **of **India **is mentioned in **Part XIV of the Constitution of India**.
 
• More specifically, it's in **Chapter II of this part, titled "Services Under the Union and the States"**.
 
• The relevant articles for the powers, functions, and responsibilities of the UPSC are primarily **Articles 315 to 323**.
 
• Here's a brief outline:
 
 
• **Article 315** speaks about the existence of the UPSC and State Public Service Commissions.
 
• **Article 316** covers the appointment and term of office of members.
 
• **Article 317** provides conditions for removal of a member.
 
• **Article 318** is about the power to make regulations about the commission's workings.
 
• **Article 319** discusses restrictions on the employment of commission members after ceasing to hold office.
 
• **Article 320 **describes the functions of the Public Service Commissions.
 
• **Article 321** authorizes extension of functions of Public Service Commissions.
 
• **Article 322 **relates to expenses of the Public Service Commissions.
 
• **Article 323 **speaks about the reports of Public Service Commissions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Part XVII of the Constitution of India** is titled **"Official Language"**.

 
 
• It contains **Articles 343 to 351**, which deal with the languages that should be used for the **Union government, for the states, and for communication between the two.**
 
 
 
• **Part XV of the Constitution of India** is titled **"Elections"**.
 
 
• It contains **Articles 324 to 329A,** which deal with the provisions related to the **election process in India.**
 
 
 
• **Part XVI of the Constitution of India** is titled** "Special Provisions Relating to Certain Classes"**.
 
 
• It contains Articles** 330 to 342,** which address provisions related to **Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Anglo-Indians. **

questions.question: Mawsynram in the southern ranges of the _______ receives the highest average rainfall in the world.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Khasi hills**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Mawsynram is located approximately 16 kilometers west of Cherrapunji, another location famous for high rainfall. However, Mawsynram receives a higher annual average rainfall, making it the wettest place on Earth.
 
• The Khasi Hills form part of the Meghalaya subtropical forests eco-region. Together with the Garo and Jaintia Hills, these form the state of Meghalaya, meaning "abode of the clouds" in Sanskrit.
 
• Khasi Hills and Mawsynram's high rainfall can be attributed to a phenomenon called "orographic lift". As air from the Bay of Bengal moves over the area, it's forced to rise due to the high elevations. The air cools and condenses, forming clouds and resulting in heavy rainfall.
 
• Mawsynram is noted for its "living bridges", formed by guiding the roots of rubber fig trees across rivers and streams, serving the local population's traversal needs.
 
• The Khasi Hills are also known for unique biodiversity. The region is home to numerous endemic species of flora and fauna.
 
• The Khasi Hills region features a matrilineal social system, which is quite unique in the context of India's predominately patrilineal society. This means descent and ancestry are traced through the female lineage.
 
• The Khasi Hills Autonomous District Council (KHADC) governs the Khasi Hills. This special provision, under the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution of India, allows for the preservation of tribal autonomy in matters of culture and traditional practices.
 
• Mawsynram's wet climate has resulted in a primarily grassland-type ecosystem, with large patches of remnant sacred grove forests which are protected by traditional tribal laws.
 
• The average annual rainfall at Mawsynram is about 11,871 millimeters (467.4 in), compared to Cherrapunji's 11,777 millimeters (463.7 in)

 
 

 [IMAGE: https://www.meghalaya.gov.in/sites/default/files/maps/ekh.jpg]

questions.question: Himalaya Frontal Fault separates Shivalik from ________.
questions.solution:

__
 
• ** The Himalaya Frontal Fault separates the Shivalik Range from the Great Plains of northern India, which is also known as the Indo-Gangetic Plains.**
 
• The Shivalik Range is a low mountain range located at the southern foothills of the Himalayas, while the Great Plains are a vast alluvial plain that stretches across northern India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh.
 
• The fault zone is characterized by intense seismic activity and has been responsible for several major earthquakes in the region over the past century.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** The Small Himalaya** is a mountain range that is part of the larger Himalayan mountain system.

 
 
• It is located south of the Great Himalaya Range, and it runs parallel to it for much of its length.
 
• The Small Himalaya extends over a distance of approximately 1,500 km from the east to the west, covering parts of Nepal, Bhutan, and northern India.
 
 
 
• **The Central Himalayas** is a region in the Himalayan mountain range that stretches across the northern parts of India, Nepal, and Bhutan.
 
 
• It is located between the eastern and western Himalayas and is characterized by its high peaks, glaciers, and deep river valleys.
 
• The Central Himalayas region includes several important mountain ranges, such as the Dhauladhar Range, the Pir Panjal Range, and the Mahabharat Range.
 
 
 
• **The Great Himalayas** is the highest mountain range in the world, located in South Asia, spanning over** 2,400 km (1,500 mi) across five countries: Bhutan, India, Nepal, China, and Pakistan. The range is home to the world's highest peaks, including Mount Everest, K2, and Kangchenjunga.**

questions.question: Cotton requires ______ temperature, light rainfall or irrigation, ______ frost-free days and bright sun-shine for its growth.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**high, 210.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Cotton thrives in **high temperatures**, which promotes** optimal growth and development.**
 
• It requires l**ight rainfall **or proper irrigation to provide the necessary moisture for its growth.
 
• Cotton cultivation requires a significant number of frost-free days,** typically around 210, **to ensure the plant's survival and uninterrupted growth.
 
• **Bright sunshine** is crucial for cotton plants as they require ample sunlight for photosynthesis, which is essential for their growth and the production of cotton fibres.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kharif crops**

 
 
• Kharif Crops are** planted at the onset of the South-West monsoon,** primarily in** India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh,** during the rainy season. 
 
• The sowing of these crops takes place between the months of **June and July. **
 
• Upon reaching maturity, typically in October, these crops are **harvested in the Autumn season. **
 
• Examples of Kharif crops include **rice, cotton, corn, sugarcane, turmeric, pigeon pea, and more.**
 
 
 
• **Rabi crops**
 
 
• Rabi Crops are** cultivated during the winter season **in regions with a subtropical climate.
 
• They include important crops like **wheat, barley, oats, chickpeas, and peas.**
 
• The **Sowing of Rabi crops** takes place between **October and December**.
 
• These crops** require cooler temperatures and lesser rainfall** compared to Kharif crops.
 
• Rabi crops play a crucial role in ensuring food security and contribute significantly to the agricultural economy.
 
 
 
• **Zaid crops**
 
 
• Zaid Crops are **grown during the summer season** in regions with a **tropical climate**.
 
• These crops are typically** cultivated between the months of March and June.**
 
• Zaid crops are known for their **quick growth and shorter duration** compared to Kharif and Rabi crops.
 
• Examples of Zaid crops include **cucumber, watermelon, bitter gourd, and cowpea.**
 
• These crops are often irrigated using modern techniques and are harvested before the onset of the monsoon season.

questions.question: The 2025 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded for the discoveries concerning _______________________________.

options.text: Peripheral immune tolerance and regulatory T cells
Understanding of IPEX syndrome in gene therapy
The role of central tolerance in the thymus

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Peripheral immune tolerance and regulatory T cells.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **The 2025 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded for discoveries concerning peripheral immune tolerance and regulatory T cells (Tregs).**

 
 
• Shimon Sakaguchi's 1995 discovery revealed regulatory T cells (Tregs) as key players in immune tolerance, challenging previous beliefs.
 
• Mary E. Brunkow and Fred Ramsdell's 2001 discovery of the FOXP3 gene was pivotal in understanding Treg function and its link to autoimmune diseases like IPEX syndrome.
 
• The work has significantly advanced our understanding of autoimmune diseases, cancer immunotherapy, and organ transplant success.
 
• Treg dysfunction can lead to autoimmune diseases, while excessive Treg activity can suppress the immune response against tumors in cancer.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__** 

__
 
• The*** 2025 Nobel Prizes ***were awarded across five categories, highlighting achievements in quantum physics, materials science, immunology, literature, and peace.

 
 
• **Physics Prize:**

 
 
• Awarded to** John Clarke, Michel H. Devoret, and John M. Martinis** for their work in **macroscopic quantum mechanical tunneling and energy quantization in electric circuits**, showcasing quantum mechanics at a macroscopic scale.
 
• Their work enabled advances in quantum computing, cryptography, and quantum sensors.
 
 
 
• **Chemistry Prize:**
 
 
• Awarded to** Susumu Kitagawa, Richard Robson, and Omar M. Yaghi** for their development of **metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), materials with vast internal surface areas** for various applications such as water harvesting, carbon capture, and toxic gas storage.
 
 
 
• **Literature Prize:**
 
 
• Awarded to L**ászló Krasznahorkai **for his** visionary works, including "Satantango**", which explore themes of apocalyptic terror, chaos, and human isolation.
 
• Known for long, complex sentences and dark, philosophical narratives.
 
 
 
• **Peace Prize:**
 
 
• Awarded to **Maria Corina Machado**, a** Venezuelan leader **and symbol of democratic resistance against authoritarianism in Venezuela, emphasizing "ballots over bullets" and leading the opposition.
 
• Praised for her courage despite life-threatening risks and for unifying the opposition around democratic principles.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• PM Narendra Modi virtually laid the foundation stone for the first Integrated Aqua Park in Nagaland, at Tzudikong in Mokokchung district.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• The Aqua Park will serve as a hub for fisheries-related development and will be the first of its kind in Nagaland.
 
• It will focus on **fish and seed production** and act as a comprehensive resource centre for the fisheries sector.
 
• The facility aims to provide **market linkages, quality inputs, and equitable pricing** for fishery products.
 
• It will create **new livelihood opportunities**, empower educated unemployed youth, and promote sustainable growth in fisheries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Integrated Aqua Park**__: A comprehensive facility aimed at enhancing fish production, seed quality, and overall development in the fisheries sector.
 
• __**Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY)**__: A flagship central government scheme to promote fisheries, ensure sustainable growth, and boost livelihoods.
 
• __**Livelihood opportunities**__: Employment avenues generated for youth and local communities through fisheries development activities.
 
• __**Market linkages**__: Systems connecting producers to buyers, ensuring fair prices and improved access to markets for fishery products.

questions.question: Kelucharan Mohapatra is a famous personality associated with which of the following dance forms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odissi.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kelucharan Mohapatra** is a **renowned Indian classical dancer** and **choreographer** who is primarily associated with the **dance form of Odissi.**
 
• He is considered as one of the pioneers who **revived and popularized Odissi** dance in the **20th century.**
 
• Kelucharan Mohapatra was born in **1926 **in the state of Odisha and started his dance training at a young age under the guidance of his** guru, Pankaj Charan Das.**
 
• He has received several awards and honors for his contribution to the field of dance, including the **Padma Vibhushan,** the second-highest civilian award in India.
 
• **Kathak, Chhau, and Manipuri **are also prominent Indian classical dance forms, but they are not directly associated with Kelucharan Mohapatra.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kathak** is a dance form that originated in **northern India **and is known for its **intricate footwork and graceful movements.**

 
 
• It has both **Hindu and Islamic influences **and is often performed to classical music.
 
 
 
• **Chhau** is a tribal dance form that is popular in the eastern states of India, particularly in **Jharkhand, Odisha, and West Bengal.**
 
 
• It involves **elaborate costumes **and masks and is often performed during **festivals and religious ceremonies.**
 
 
 
• **Manipuri** is a dance form that originated in the **northeastern state of Manipur **and is known for its **fluid and graceful movements.**
 
 
• It is often performed to classical music and has both **Hindu and Buddhist influences.**

questions.question: Navreh is the lunar new year that is celebrated in which of the following states/union territories?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jammu and Kashmir**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Navreh

 
 
• It is the lunar new year that is celebrated in Kashmir.
 
• It is the Sanskrit word ‘Nav-Varsha’ from which the word ‘Navreh’ has been derived.
 
• It falls on the first day of the Chaitra Navratri.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Ugadi

 
 
• The festival of Ugadi is celebrated on the first day of Chaitra month as per the Hindu calendar
 
• Ugadi, also known as Yugadi, is a renowned South Indian festival mainly celebrated in Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, and Telangana to commemorate the beginning of a new year.
 
• For Ugadi, doors in homes are adorned with mango leaf decorations called toranalu or Torana in Kannada
 
 
 
• Vishu
 
 
• It is a Hindu festival celebrated in the Indian state of Kerala, Tulu Nadu region in Karnataka, Mahé district of Union Territory of Pondicherry, neighbouring areas of Tamil Nadu, and their diaspora communities.
 
• "Vishu" means "equal" in the Sanskrit language.
 
• It is called Malayali New Year.
 
• The festival marks the first day of Medam, the ninth month in the solar calendar followed in Kerala.
 
 
 
• Pana Sankranti
 
 
• Oriya New Year is also known as Pana Sankranti and it is observed as the first day of the Oriya Calendar.
 
• It is also known as ‘Maha Vishuba Sankranti,’ ‘Maha Sankranti,’ and ‘Mesha Sankranti’ is a festival that is widely celebrated across Odisha as the traditional New Year
 
• Pana Sankranti is named after ‘Pana,’ the main fruit drink which is prepared in Odisha’s traditional culture.
